description: Issue #828: BaseCRUDVM.RejectUnresolvableFileAttachmentReferences used to feed ResolveFileAttachmentIdsForCaller's resolved-id set straight into ApplyFileAttachmentResolution even when the underlying batched FileAttachment resolution QUERY had thrown (SQL Server's 2100-parameter cap under EF Core 10's default multi-parameter Contains() translation, a timeout, a transient connection drop, ...). An exception collapsed to an EMPTY resolved set, indistinguishable from 'the query succeeded and none of these ids exist'. For a posted ISubFile collection whose every item happened to be a resolution candidate -- the ordinary case, since editing an entity normally re-posts its own children too -- every item was then dropped by ApplyFileAttachmentResolution's per-item narrowing, emptying the WHOLE posted collection, which routes into DoEditPreparePart2's empty-collection branch: it physically deletes EVERY existing child row for that parent while DoEdit reports success. The fix adds a Succeeded flag to the resolution result and rejects the WHOLE request when resolution itself failed (MSD.AddModelError, nothing persisted) BEFORE ApplyFileAttachmentResolution ever runs -- the same whole-request-rejection contract the pre-existing required-FK-with-no-prior-value path already used (#815 sixth/seventh round). This mutant neutralizes the new guard (`if (!resolution.Succeeded)` -> `if (!resolution.Succeeded && false)`, compile-preserving) in the SYNC method only, reproducing the exact pre-fix fallthrough into ApplyFileAttachmentResolution with an empty resolved set. Checked against FileAttachmentResolutionFailureGateTests828.cs's DoEdit_ resolution-failure test, which seeds a Product with two pre-existing FileAttachment-backed children, arms a DbCommandInterceptor that throws on every SELECT against the FileAttachment table, and re-posts the SAME two children unchanged. Under the mutant, the guard never fires, both children get dropped from the posted collection (LoadExistingSubItemFileIds cannot restore them -- the posted items carry no matching existing-row id, same construction pattern as the sibling #815 SQLite fixtures), DoEditPreparePart2's empty-collection branch deletes both real rows, and DoEdit reports success (vm.MSD stays empty) -- which is exactly what the test's first assertion (the caller must be told the request failed) catches. The async counterpart (DoEditAsync_...) and the large-legitimate-batch test (DoEdit_CandidateCountAboveBatchSize_...) are unaffected by this mutant, since it only touches the sync method's guard and the batch-size test never arms the interceptor at all -- both serve as positive controls proving the mutation's blast radius is exactly the declared line, not the whole fix.

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.Test.VM.FileAttachm: #828: the caller must be told the request failed when resolution itself failed

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured against a clean checkout (stale demo.db under bin/ removed first) with the mutant patch applied: 'Assert.IsTrue failed. #828: the caller must be told the request failed when resolution itself failed — a dependency failure must never be reported as success'.
